issue.title: sase-spotify: Spotify library reads and gated playlist changes for SASE agents
issue.description: SASE agents of any provider can read Bryan's Spotify library through `sase spotify` and a `/sase_spotify` skill: every playlist, the songs in owned and collaborative playlists and Liked Songs, followed podcasts, and their recent episodes. Library data never reaches a publicly published agent chat, because the CLI enforces that boundary itself. Agents change playlists only by proposing one declarative changeset per task. Bryan reviews it as a PR-style SASE gate in the TUI or on Telegram, and only the option he approves writes to Spotify; that write is re-checked, journaled, reconciled, and verified. The new private sase-org/sase-spotify plugin ships with excellent docs, a strict test suite, and CI. It is installed and accepted end to end on athena.

payload.entry: repo phase planning evidence: `sase project create gh:sase-org/sase-spotify --visibility private --description ... --alias spotify --check --json` -> status blocked, sole blocker human_only ("propose sase project create through /sase_gate"); key gh_sase-org__sase-spotify, accent #8E67CA, checkout ~/projects/github/sase-org/sase-spotify/. Alias: docs/reference/work-units/project-spec.md says PROJECT_ALIASES are accepted in +<project> tags, so --alias spotify makes +spotify usable; kept. Variant: under the gate (SASE_GATE_COMMAND=1 => human actor) the flagless default resolves to setup=new_repo (same as --setup). Its executed steps are create_remote, checkout, identity, and manage (commit+push sase/sase.yml is_sase_managed), and none of them needs a TTY. The TTY-only init step is a handoff that apply never runs under --json; it only returns next_argv `sase init -p gh_sase-org__sase-spotify`. SSH push to GitHub works with no ssh-agent (BatchMode), so the manage push can finish unattended. --no-setup skips manage, and its plan warns not_launchable until `sase init -M`. Chose explicit --setup. Proposed gate turn: create/reject options, workspace release, branch follow-ups for create/reject/failed, plus a read-only plan-preview action.

Scaffold contract notes for later phases (deviations from the plan text, all scaffold-owned): (1) CI and pr-title trigger on `main`, the repo default branch created by sase project create, not `master`; rollout should check main CI. (2) errors.py adds one code, `config_invalid` (exit 3), for bad config files; every other code is exactly the contract table. (3) coverage fail_under=90: the scaffold measured 95.7%, already above the epic target, so propose phase "raise to 90" is satisfied. (4) TokenProvider lives in the new scaffold module tokens.py as access_token(scopes=(), *, force_refresh=False) -> str; force_refresh is the single post-401 retry. StaticTokenProvider is a test double. (5) cli/common.py (scaffold) holds parser helpers; -j/-r/-a use SUPPRESS defaults so they work at any level, so read them via json_requested()/refresh_requested() or args after app.main fills defaults. Hidden commands: auth complete -p/--pending; changes apply -b/--bundle -g/--group; changes check -b; changes close -b -s/--status {revise_requested,rejected}. --version also -V. (6) sase_bridge.notify always sends -p with -k (sase requires it), defaulting to the first note; sase dedup actions are created|plus_oned, and -S supersedes only on the create branch. (7) tests/fakes/sase_cli.py is a stateful fake sase plus a fake_sase fixture. The autouse isolated_env fixture strips every SASE_* var and relocates HOME/XDG. (8) default_config.yml ships as a comment-only (empty) layer so sase never logs "failed to load plugin default_config.yml"; skills/ holds only .gitkeep until skill-docs. (9) ui.safe_text strips all Unicode Cf (bidi, zero-width, tag-block smuggling) except ZWJ/ZWNJ.
